headline: Discussed outstanding 2023 audit items and scheduled meetings every other Wednesday starting October 21, 2026.
summary: The committee reviewed its scope and the status of the 2023 audit, including items still outstanding. Finance Director Hull will update a tracker of these items weekly and add due dates. The committee will meet every other Wednesday starting October 21, 2026.
decisions: Set the committee's meeting schedule to every other Wednesday from 6:00 to 7:30 starting October 21, 2026.

decision_evidence.quote: The Committee will meet every other Wednesday from 6:00 to 7:30 starting October 21, 2026.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, 
CONNECTICUT 
AUDIT COMMITTEE 
SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES 
6:00 PM, October 8, 2026
 
Committee Chair: 
Sarah Gallagher, Majority Ldr 
Committee Members: 
Katie Kiely, Council President 
Bob Anthony, Minority Leader 
Jeron Alston 
Rhonda Caldwell 
Alternates 
Sean Cardwell, Pro Tem 
Tasha Hunt, Majority Whip 
Tom Figlar, Minority Whip 
1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLL 
Audit Committee Meeting, October 8, 2026 – 6:00pm.  The meeting was called to order by 
Chair Gallagher at 6:07pm with the following members in attendance: 
 
In Person: 
Sarah Gallagher, Majority Ldr  
Tom Figlar, Minority Whip 
 
Remote: 
Katie Kiely, Council President  
Bob Anthony, Minority Leader 
Jeron Alston Rhonda Caldwell 
Sean Cardwell, Pro Tem 
 
Also in attendance, Finance Director Hul and Santo Carta of the audit firm CLA, 
 
2. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION 
There were 4 individuals in attendance in person and 3 online.  3 people came forward to 
give public comment.  The Public Input session was closed at 6:16pm. 
3 people gave public input 
 
3. SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA 
1. Review Scope of Committee 
Chair Gallagher provided an overview of the Committee Scope: 
- Is it not the role of the committee to do the audit. 
- The mayor is required to provide the Legislative Council and Finance Commission with 
an audit schedule/calendar covering a timeframe from: (1) the commencement of the 
process through the preliminary departmental requests; (2) follow – up information 
requests; (3) field work; (4) circulation of draft audit report and management letter; and 
(5) final audit. 
- The calendar should be developed in accordance with best practices as set forth by the 
State of Connecticut and the Office of Policy and Management of the State of 
Connecticut (OMP) and the Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA) 
- Make recommendations to the Legislative Council pertaining to the selection of an 
independent auditor for the next fiscal year in accordance with the Chater Section 4-10. 
o Auditor changes every 6 years 
- Meeting with the independent auditor during the audit period to discuss the overall scope 
of the audit plan, including the adequacy of staffing and other factors that may affect the 
effectiveness and timeliness of the audit.
- Meeting with the designee of the mayor responsible for the providing of information to 
the independent auditor and the chair of the finance committee to discuss the adequacy 
and effectiveness of the accounting and financial controls. 
- Meeting with the Mayor of their designee, any professional firms advising the Town, the 
Chair of the Finance Commission and other officials pertaining to status of any 
deficiencies in the audit process in order to address such deficiencies. 
- Appraise the effectiveness and completeness of the audit effort. 
- Evaluate the financial management, accounting and control practices of the town in 
coordination with the Finance Committee and the Finance Commission. 
- Recommend to the legislative Council the scope and conditions of the audit for the next 
fiscal year. 
 
2. Committee Calendar and Meeting Cadence 
 
The Committee will meet every other Wednesday from 6:00 to 7:30 starting October 21, 
2026. 
 
3. Briefing from Administration on 2023/2024 Audits and beyond 
 
Director Hull provided the committee with an update on collected and outstanding items 
being reviewed related to the 2023 audits. See attached spreadsheet. 
 
- Councilwoman Caldwell requested a list of adjusted journal entries that did not reconcile. 
- Director Hull will update the spreadsheet of items each week and add the due date for 
each item. 
 
4. Report/Briefing from CLA and CBIZ 
 
Santo Carta from CLA provided the committee with an update of the 2023 audit and the largest 
outstanding items. See attached spreadsheet. 
5. Other Information Requests  
 
- Plan for addressing 2024, 2025 and 2026 audit mapping out where we are in collecting 
the information needed for these audits and the process of how they will fit together so 
that we do not get further behind. 
- CLA/CBIZ Audit Scope with Required Timeline. 
- List of adjusted journal entries that did not reconcile between the close of 2023 and the 
opening of 2024. 
- Timeline from CLA for town and BOE on when they will get the information and what 
they need to do to get it. 
- Finance Director Hull will add due dates to the items on the tracker. 
- Set targets for what can be accomplished by the next meeting. 
- Monthly expenditures, revenues, and YTDs 
- Ask for Finance Committee - Internal report from BOE on their capital projects and 
grants, including if there was money left over.
o School Board Committee is meeting on October 22nd – they will work to 
determine the various dollars for the various projects. 
 
4. ADJOURN 
Chair Gallagher adjourned the meeting at approximately 7:50pm
